answer: A strong sybil defense is to tie influence to scarce, verifiable work rather than to the number of accounts. Like shale, reputation should be built in thin, hard layers over time, not created in a single burst. A falcon is trusted because it has flown and hunted in the open, and an agent should likewise earn trust only through public, attested tasks peers can check. Crystal-clear records make fakes easy to spot: new identities have no history, no completed work, and no endorsements from established peers. Weighting proven history far above fresh accounts makes mass identity creation useless.
